admission_fixture_rules: New candidate objects are literal raw request examples (no tuple_ref). Provider state is a test-authority observation, never a serialized permission. Nonfinite numbers and language inspection failures are not encoded as invalid JSON here; these vectors use literal JSON-compatible values. Every admission failure has Core/Host count zero. Unknown-key test observations outside read_call_result are not public echoes. JCS examples for admission bodies contain only scalar-safe ASCII after sanitization, so the exact encoding is supplied and independently reproducible without a general JCS implementation.
budget_fixture_rule: Byte lengths are explicit inputs to the final budget decision stage, not measured encodings of the symbolic IR fixture. Fixed-width accounting is specified in R06; later implementation must independently encode the full envelope.
diagnostic_ref: specs/read-contract.md R04 and R07; specs/public-contract-decisions.json diagnostic_design_registry
digest_primitive_rule: SHA values computed solely with standard-library SHA256 over explicit preimage bytes; ASCII-only JSON examples already have a stated JCS preimage. No general JCS implementation, Core code or product test ran; these primitive inputs do not claim container/Capsule format validity.
expected_notation: ReadCallResult four discriminants and all null sibling fields are exact assertions. Old symbolic IR cases and lawful Envelope-size stage cases use an explicitly labelled assertion projection inside envelope; observation_scope is test notation, never a wire field. New admission rejection/control/transport payloads are full closed values. Root project returns ReadProjection, not a fictitious ReadCallResult. Digest/Writer/declaration/package-set primitive cases explicitly mark read_call_result=null and keep their own operation assertions; wrapping them in a ReadEnvelope would invent a public disclosure operation. All original 54 IDs remain; every Read adapter case has the new result layer.
fixture_rules: Named fixture preconditions are test-authority assumptions, never accepted serialized Core/Host authority. An override is a dotted-path replacement; {$delete:true} deletes that one field. Fixture metadata is not serialized public input. Resolve overrides ending in tuple_ref first, expand each named tuple into the enclosing tuple property and remove tuple_ref, then apply all remaining dotted overrides. Resolve request.handle_ref=issued-handle:1 to the final fixture.handle and remove handle_ref before decoding the public request. The default node scenario uses a captured Uint8Array whose Core adapter result is the declared fixture; the root scenario passes that Core snapshot directly. Browser input representation is explicit. Fixture Core/Host witness labels, admission state and registry flags are test-authority observations, not fields supplied by asset callers. Unmentioned Host correlation identifiers match the resolved request/snapshot. A registry_matches_overridden_handle=true case means an actually issued older/different record, not attacker-editing a live record. Core data arrays describe Core-owned IR read nodes by stable ID; generated Canonical IR schema fixtures will supply exact nodes. Modes preserve listed order; assertion fields not listed in an expected object are outside that vector observation, never default success.
